subject: Reconcile: duplicate hourly ingest counts affecting May 16 invoice
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@optiscale.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected duplicate counts during 05/16 hourly ingest window - urgent

Hi Soojin,

We're reconciling our May 16 usage and see a ~38k token spike between 03:00-04:00 UTC that doesn't line up with our application telemetry. The attached screenshot shows our dashboard vs the usage export. This is outside our normal ingest pattern and will push us over the monthly threshold.

Can Redwood confirm whether there was an ingestion duplication or replay on your side? We need to know ASAP because our AR team runs payments on Friday and we can't pay for unexpected duplicates.

I've attached a screenshot and a short snippet of our client request IDs (below) — happy to share more.

Sample request ids: 6bf4d2a2-9c1b-4c3a, 6bf4d2a2-9c1b-4c3a (appears twice)

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of Finance, OptiScale
finance@optiscale.com
Attachment: optiscale_screenshot.png
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@optiscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate counts during 05/16 hourly ingest window - urgent

Hi Julia — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. Sorry for the disruption.

I'm looping in Ben from billing and Jordan from your AE team so we can triage quickly. Initial ask: can you forward a short sample of raw request IDs and timestamps (a handful is fine) and confirm whether the client SDK was retrying around that window? Ben, could you pull a telemetry export for 2028-05-16 02:45–04:15 UTC (UTC) and look for duplicated request IDs / parallel session artifacts?

We can temporarily hold the invoice or mark the disputed line while we investigate — please confirm whether OptiScale needs a provisional credit before your Friday payment run.

I'll keep you posted with timelines.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Julia Park <julia@optiscale.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T12:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate counts during 05/16 hourly ingest window - urgent

Thanks Soojin / Julia — I've pulled the initial telemetry slice. Preliminary findings: there is a pattern consistent with duplicated upstream requests between 03:05–03:22 UTC where a spike of near-identical request IDs (same prefix) is present across 3 routing hosts. That typically indicates a client-side retry storm (idempotency key not honored at the SDK layer) or a transient proxy that replayed requests.

Attached: redwood_telemetry_sample.log (excerpt with timestamps and server-side request ids). I've also exported a full trace to our shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cTelemetryExports/optiscale-may16 — folder contains per-host logs and token counts per request.

Action items I propose:
- We mark the disputed invoice line and recommend a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens (we can calculate exact amount after you confirm sample IDs).
- If OptiScale confirms the duplicates come from their SDK/proxy, we will provide a one-time credit and guidance to prevent recurrence.
- If duplicates originated from our routing layer (unlikely per first-pass), we will issue full credit and perform a postmortem.

Julia — can you confirm the sample request IDs include the ones you pasted? If you can share 5–10 more raw IDs (and any request headers like X-Client-Request-Id), that will let us match server-side rows exactly.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_telemetry_sample.log
From: Julia Park <julia@optiscale.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: OptiScale Finance <finance@optiscale.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate counts during 05/16 hourly ingest window - urgent

Ben — thanks for digging in so fast. I've attached a small CSV with 8 sample request IDs and timestamps (pasted below) — all showing the same id repeated twice from our side. We did see a proxy redeploy around 03:10 UTC but didn't think it would replay at-scale.

Samples:
- 6bf4d2a2-9c1b-4c3a, 2028-05-16T03:11:02Z
- 6bf4d2a2-9c1b-4c3a, 2028-05-16T03:11:03Z
- 9f1a3c8e-2b7d-4a44, 2028-05-16T03:14:18Z
- 9f1a3c8e-2b7d-4a44, 2028-05-16T03:14:19Z

We have an AP run scheduled Friday (2028-05-19) — if Redwood can confirm provisional credit by EOD Thursday that would allow us to proceed without blocking payment. Otherwise we'll place the invoice on hold and follow up.

Let me know what you need from our engineering team.

— Julia
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@optiscale.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate counts during 05/16 hourly ingest window - urgent

Julia — Kimberly from Finance here. We can place OptiScale's May invoice on payment hold until the dispute is resolved, but for audit and SOX controls we need a short adjustment memo that both parties sign-off on before we issue a provisional credit.

Soojin — could you draft a one-page memo (adjustment amount estimate + reason + follow-up steps) and share as a DocuSign link? I can review quickly. If OptiScale signs, we'll reflect a provisional credit in their account and unblock payment.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@optiscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate counts during 05/16 hourly ingest window - urgent

Julia — thanks, got the sample IDs. Ben and I matched the rows and estimate ~36,842 duplicated tokens attributable to the retry/replay. Pending your engineering confirmation, we'll prepare an adjustment memo for a one-time credit covering the duplicated tokens.

I've drafted the memo and uploaded it for signature: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/adjustment-memo-OPTISC-2314 (contains line item calculation + acceptance checkbox). Attachment: adjustment_memo_draft.docx

Next steps:
- OptiScale signs the DocuSign memo (please route to finance).
- We apply a provisional credit and mark the invoice line disputed in billing.
- Ben will follow up with a short prevention checklist (idempotency headers + proxy guidance) and our engineering team will offer a quick review with your infra if helpful.

I'll keep this thread updated once the credit posts. Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll aim to have a provisional credit reflected before your payment run on 2028-05-19.

— Soojin
